transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
A Democratic senator is asking the White House for immediate answers about a new television
ad featuring President Trump.
The ad says it's paid for by the U.S. government.
NPR's Tamara Keith reports the White House defends it as educational and patriotic.
The ad features President Trump's voice and a splashy montage of images of the president.
Phrases including "Largest Tax Cut in History" flash on the screen, as the song providing
the soundtrack to the 30-second ad repeats the phrase, "Love Me."
"America will never be a communist country."
In a letter demanding answers, Democratic senator from New Hampshire Maggie Hassan says
the ad appears to run afoul of federal prohibitions against using government funds for propaganda.
A White House spokesperson described the ad as a "public service announcement."
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
The White House network video pool is back in operation.
This morning marked the first time it had been in action since President Trump banned
three news outlets in a showdown over media access.
A judge temporarily struck down Trump's ban of CNN, MS Now and Politico yesterday, but
other TV networks continued to suspend pool coverage in solidarity until the White House
explicitly allowed CNN to rejoin the pool.
Chinese President Xi Jinping wrapped up his visit to the U.S. today.
Trump says he and Xi will meet again in China in November and Xi will come to the U.S. again
in December.
And PR's Emily Feng reports.
Trump and Xi Jinping visited the National Archives on the last day of the Chinese leaders'
state visit, where Trump said his meetings with Xi the day before were very good.
Trump then posted on social media that he and Xi will meet again at the Asia-Pacific
Economic Coordination Summit in southern China in November, as well as in Miami, where the
2020 leaders' summit will be held the month after.
That would mean the two men will have formally met in person four times this year, an ambitious
diplomatic push to stabilize ties despite real tensions.
Asked whether the war with Iran was raised with China, Trump nodded in acknowledgment
but didn't offer details.
China has been a big supporter of Iran, buying up the majority of Iran's oil exports before
the war.
Emily Feng, NPR News Washington.
People on the big island of Hawaii are under a hurricane watch today.
NPR's Bill Chappell reports Hurricane NOLO could bring feet of rain.
Hurricane NOLO is not expected to make landfall on Hawaii's big island, but it's coming
close enough to drop about two feet of rain in some areas over the weekend, according
to the National Hurricane Center.
That can cause dangerous flooding and mudslides.
As of Friday morning, NOLO's maximum winds were around 85 miles per hour.
It's expected to strengthen into a major storm.
Forecasters say it will also move very slowly, increasing the risk of floods from sustained,
heavy rain.
Schools are closed on Maui and the big island.
Some are being used as shelters for people seeking safety.
Bill Chappell, NPR News This is NPR.
New Jersey's Democratic Lieutenant Governor has resigned after the governor demanded he
step down over allegations of inappropriate behavior with women.
Democratic Governor Mikey Sherrill had given Lieutenant Governor Dale Caldwell an ultimatum
that he resigned by the end of the day.
A law firm hired by Sherrill issued a report yesterday accusing Caldwell of making a sexually
charged comment to a female staff member and trying to get a promotion for a state employee
he was dating.
The parent company of Florida's Brightline Railroad has filed for bankruptcy protection,
NPR's Joel Rose reports its passenger trains will continue operating during the restructuring.
Brightline has announced a plan to restructure its $5.5 billion debt load in Chapter 11 bankruptcy
proceedings.
The privately owned railroad opened with much fanfare in South Florida eight years ago and
began running its neon yellow trains between Miami and Orlando in 2023.
Ridership has been growing, but not fast enough to make the numbers work.
Brightline says its operating company is not part of the bankruptcy filing and that Florida
trains will continue running.
Still, the filing casts doubt on the future of privately owned passenger rail in the U.S.,
including Brightline West, which aims to connect Las Vegas and Southern California.
Joel Rose, NPR News.
The robotic spacecraft that failed to rescue an aging NASA telescope has plunged back to
Earth less than three months after launching.
It re-entered the atmosphere overnight, bringing the $30 million salvage effort of NASA's Swift
Observatory to a close.
Swift is expected to follow in early November as its orbit steadily sinks.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Democratic senator Maggie Hassan demands White House answers about government-funded Trump campaign advertisement
White House network video pool resumes operations after judge temporarily struck down Trump's media ban
Chinese President Xi Jinping concludes U.S. state visit; Trump and Xi plan meetings in November and December
Hurricane NOLO threatens Hawaii's big island with up to two feet of rain this weekend
New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Dale Caldwell resigns after Governor Mikey Sherrill's ultimatum over misconduct allegations
Brightline Railroad parent company files Chapter 11 bankruptcy while continuing Florida passenger train operations
Failed robotic spacecraft meant to rescue NASA's Swift Observatory re-enters Earth's atmosphere after three months
